items.title: Warren Bernhardt interviewed by Monk Rowe, Bearsville, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: For Steely Dan I was the musical director or rehearsal director or whatever you called it. If Donald or Walter didn’t want to show up in the afternoon when we were setting up, I’d conduct it

ctx.x: And then he’d turn it off as soon as you get two bars into it then the click was gone, but once you establish that tempo, they were real sticklers on that. But it was a three and a half hour show. I had to change my clothes at intermission, I was just completely drenched. I’d lose ten pounds in a show. And it’s a lot of effort and a lot of music, and there wasn’t a bad song in it. Opening tune: “Aja.” I mean that’s like Simon & Garfunkel starting a set with “Bridge Over Troubled Water” you just didn’t do that.…

lot of guitar. Many guitars and very little piano. Okay, you play here and then stop. You know. And then you play here and then stop. And that can change from night to night. So you always have to be on your toes. But the material is always great. I mean it’s like playing with the Beatles or something. I mean the audience reaction. And you see a grandfather and a father and a son all standing by the stage all in tears during “The Boxer” or something, near the end of the show. It’s really moving. I mean I used to…
